scope: Bounded audit for one noisy binary-composition round of the Phase 3 family. Not a novelty certification or a survey of all functional-decomposition algorithms.

primary_sources.title: A Linear-Time Algorithm for Testing the Truth of Certain Quantified Boolean Formulas
locators: Theorem 1 and constructive converse, printed p. 122
primary_sources.checked: The existential 2-CNF instance is satisfiable iff no literal shares a strongly connected component with its complement.
primary_sources.use_limit: The source does not supply our composed-junta recognizer, its augmented-parity fibers, or its Boolean gate count. The source RAM-time bound is not used as a gate bound.

manual_new_deductions: All binary combinations of the old radius-r family lie within radius 2r of binary combinations of its centers.
For fixed support pair, operation and global shift flags, decoded feature consistency is a Boolean binary-constraint problem independently on each common-coordinate slice.
A fixed Boolean transitive-closure network implements those 2-SAT checks in O(2^(3k)) gates per support pair.
Together with majority decoding and mismatch counting, the outer size is O(binomial(m,k)^2*(N*m+2^(3k))).
For fixed beta<1/5, the same k and r as Phase 3 give sound acceptance, separated tubes, and exponent 1+2H(beta)+o(1).
Parity on 2k+1 address variables is a cheap missed YES instance obtained by a further XOR round.
scope_limits: One round is relative to the old family, not a fixed-point closure property of the new family.
The full GapMCSP promise is not solved; explicit YES tables are rejected.
Higher-arity constraints do not by themselves prove NP-hardness of the structured decomposition problem.
No claim is made that the particular full method satisfies a literature internal-oracle closure condition.
The elementary combination is not claimed novel.
